the_two_defenses.restore_before_serve: durable.restore_for_serve() (bounded retries, default 3 x 5s) evaluates the gate BEFORE the server serves; the success predicate is error==None AND integrity_verified!=False. On exhaustion the gate CLOSES (durable.serve_gate().restored False, surfaced verbatim at /api/health durable.serve_gate) and the process serves DEGRADED: the boot snapshot and EVERY snapshot refuse (typed 'restore gate closed') and run creation refuses 503 RESTORE_GATE_CLOSED. The port still binds (the R420b health-check lesson) and a background retry thread re-attempts restore every 60s so a long outage heals without a container restart. The swallow-and-serve boot path (restore failure printed, serve anyway, boot snapshot pushed) was the EXACT 176->34 mechanism — now machine-blocked.
the_two_defenses.shrink_guard: durable._shrink_violations() compares the payload a snapshot would push against the durable branch HEAD before ANY copy/commit: the branch's session_id set (sessions.json), share-id set (shares.json) and every append-only ledger line (worker_forensics/*.jsonl, model_routing/ledger.jsonl) must SURVIVE. A smaller-or-empty snapshot over a larger durable state is refused, typed 'shrink guard blocked snapshot: ...' with per-file violation details riding durable.last_snapshot.shrink_guard. Escape hatch DURABLE_ALLOW_SHRINK=1 exists for operator-mandated resyncs and is RECORDED at every layer (snapshot report, snapshot_log.jsonl line fields shrink_override/shrink_violations, commit message suffix [shrink-override]) — never a silent shrink (Art. XV/XXV).
the_two_defenses.restore_symmetry: the guard's counterpart, same round: restore() now re-materializes model_routing/ledger.jsonl (append-only merge by request_id — the EXACT file the incident erased) and copies model_routing/state.json + transport_capability/capability_state.json copy-when-absent (local stays the live authority; never regressed by the branch copy). Without this the guard would deadlock production (branch ⊄ local forever) and the graft-v4 repair would be re-erased by the next fresh-container snapshot. The end-to-end healing loop is measured in-test: restore -> gate opens -> first post-restore snapshot is a superset and pushes the union.
